- Underside of a soybean leaf
- Numerous small, dark brown spots/lesions scattered across the surface
- Some chlorosis/yellowing of surrounding tissue
- Spots appear small, possibly slightly raised, scattered densely

Top candidates: **Soybean_rust**, **Septoria_brown_spot**, **Bacterial_Pustule**

Now I have enough information to make my assessment. Let me synthesize:

**Test image observations:**
- Underside of a soybean leaf (white raised veins visible, blue cloth background at bottom left)
- Numerous small, dark brown to brownish-black spots scattered densely across the leaf surface
- Background leaf tissue shows yellowing/chlorosis between spots
- Some spots appear to cluster into larger blotchy areas
- No white powdery coating, no fuzzy/hairy growth, no pustule openings visible

**Elimination reasoning:**
- Soybean_rust: Spots would have visible pustule openings (uredinia); reference shows tan-brown pustules — test image spots are darker and more solid
- Bacterial_Pustule: Reference shows reddish-brown spots with raised light-colored pustule centers especially on undersides — test image spots are flatter and darker brown/black
- Frogeye: Spots have gray centers with distinct reddish-brown borders — not matching
- Downy_mildew: Would show tan/gray fuzzy tufts on underside — not present
- Cercospora: Shows large purple/bronze blotches, not small discrete spots
- Powdery_Mildew: White powdery coating — not present

**Best match — Septoria_brown_spot:**
- Small, irregularly shaped dark brown lesions on both leaf surfaces (especially underside)
- Adjacent lesions coalesce into larger irregular blotches (seen in test image)
- Associated leaf yellowing expanding beyond necrotic regions
- Disease progresses from lower canopy upward
- Overall spot size, color, and density match closely
